name: Motorized Bicycle
description: Kansas's moped category: a two- or three-wheeled device propelled by human power, a helper motor or both, with a motor of no more than 3.5 brake horsepower (2,625 W), an automatic transmission and a top design speed of 30 mph. An electric two-wheeler under those limits that isn't an electric-assisted bicycle lands here.

restrictions.rule: Two tandem wheels or three wheels, propelled by human power, a helper motor or both; pedals are optional (Kansas Statutes Annotated §§8-126(y), 8-1439a)
Its motor produces no more than 3.5 brake horsepower (2,625 W), and it has an automatic transmission (Kansas Statutes Annotated §§8-126(y), 8-1439a)
A maximum design speed of no more than 30 mph (Kansas Statutes Annotated §§8-126(y), 8-1439a)
One exceeding any of these limits is titled and registered as a motorcycle instead
Not a motor vehicle under Kansas law
Riders need a driver's license of any class, or must be 15 or older and pass the written and vision exams for a motorized bicycle license
Riders and passengers under 18 must wear a motorcycle helmet
Titled and registered with the county treasurer, certifying it meets the motorized bicycle limits; insurance isn't required
Follows the rules for riding bicycles on roadways, keeping as near the right side as practicable when slower than traffic
